the role of the pore-forming Listeriolysinin in the regulation of intracellular calcium signalling and its impact on cellular responses to subsequent stimuli.

LLO is a central player in the host-pathogen interplay, which is able to induce a variety of cellular responses, but also to render cells refractory to subsequent Ca 2 + -induced signalling.

the toxin Listeriolysine O (LLO) is a central player in the infection of Listeria monocytogenes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
L.m renders cells resistant to Ca 2+ signalling through LLO-induced depletion of intracellular stores.
L. monocytogene renders cells inert to calcium signalling via LLO-induced depletion of intracellular calcium stores.
L.m renders cells inert to calcium signaling via LLO induced depletions of intracellular Ca2+ stores.
The main takeaway from our work is that
LLO induces Ca depletion in host cells which in turn renders them refractory to subsequent Ca mobilizations.
LLO is a potent inducer of Ca mobilization, but that it also induces cellular responses that render the host cell insensitive to Ca mobilization.
LLO induces depletion of intracellular stores of Ca and that this effect is a key factor in the ability of L.m to evade the host cell's Ca signalling system.
